functional_requirements.text: The clock input [CLK_I] MUST coordinate all activities for the internal logic within the WISHBONE interface. All WISHBONE output signals MUST be registered at the rising edge of [CLK_I]. All WISHBONE input signals MUST be stable before the rising edge of [CLK_I].

The reset input [RST_I] forces the WISHBONE interface to restart. All internal self-starting state machines MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I].
[RST_I] MUST be asserted for at least one complete clock cycle on all WISHBONE interfaces.
[RST_I] MAY be asserted for more than one clock cycle, and MAY be asserted indefinitely.

The MASTER signals [STB_O] and [CYC_O] MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I], and MUST stay in the negated state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I]. The state of all other MASTER signals is undefined in response to a reset cycle.
All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active HIGH logic.

MASTER interfaces MUST assert [CYC_O] for the duration of SINGLE READ / WRITE, BLOCK, and RMW cycles. [CYC_O] MUST be asserted no later than the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the assertion of [STB_O]. [CYC_O] MUST be negated no earlier than the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the negation of [STB_O].
MASTER interfaces MAY assert [CYC_O] indefinitely. (Note: keeping [CYC_O] asserted may lead to arbitration problems — RECOMMENDATION 3.05.)
SLAVE interfaces MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated. However, SLAVE interfaces MUST always respond to SYSCON signals.

Standard handshake — in standard mode the cycle termination signals [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] MUST be generated in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I]. The MASTER asserts [STB_O] and waits for one of [ACK_I], [ERR_I], or [RTY_I] before negating [STB_O].
MASTER interfaces MUST qualify the following signals with [STB_O]: [ADR_O], [DAT_O()], [SEL_O()], [WE_O], and [TAGN_O].
SLAVE interfaces MUST qualify the following signals with [ACK_O], [ERR_O], or [RTY_O]: [DAT_O()].
If a SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, then the SLAVE MUST NOT assert more than one of the following signals at any time: [ACK_O], [ERR_O] or [RTY_O].
SLAVE interfaces MUST be designed so that the [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] signals are asserted and negated in response to the assertion and negation of [STB_I].
As a minimum, the MASTER interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_I], [CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], and [STB_O].
As a minimum, the SLAVE interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], and [RST_I]. All other signals are optional.
MASTER interfaces MUST be designed to operate normally when the SLAVE interface holds [ACK_I] in the asserted state.
All user defined tags MUST be assigned a TAG TYPE. Furthermore, they MUST adhere to the timing specifications given in this document for the indicated TAG TYPE.
All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support SINGLE READ or SINGLE WRITE cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 (READ) / 3.2.3 and 3.2.4 (WRITE).
All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support BLOCK cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.2.
All MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support RMW cycles MUST conform to the timing requirements given in section 3.4.

Data organization MUST conform to the ordering indicated in Figure 3-15. Data organization on 64-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-18. Data organization on 32-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-19. Data organization on 16-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-20. Data organization on 8-bit ports MUST conform to Figure 3-21.
All WISHBONE Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST support WISHBONE Classic bus cycles.
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support [CTI_I()] and [CTI_O()] signals MUST at least support the Classic cycle [CTI_IO()=3'b000] and the End-of-Cycle [CTI_IO()=3'b111].
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that are designed to support a limited number of burst types MUST complete the unsupported cycles as though they were WISHBONE Classic cycle, i.e. [CTI_IO()=3'b000].

A cycle terminates when both the cycle termination signal and [STB_I], [STB_O] is asserted. Even if [ACK_O], [ACK_I] is asserted, the other signals are only valid when [STB_O], [STB_I] is also asserted.
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that support incrementing burst cycles MUST support the [BTE_O()] and [BTE_I()] signals.
MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that are designed to support a limited number of burst extensions MUST complete the unsupported cycles as though they were WISHBONE Classic cycle, i.e. [CTI_IO()=3'b000].
A MASTER MUST set End-Of-Burst on [CTI_O()] to signal the end of the current burst (last beat of a burst is [CTI_O()=3'b111]).

A MASTER signaling an incrementing burst MUST initiate another cycle; the next cycle MUST be the same operation (either read or write), the select lines [SEL_O()] MUST have the same value, the address array [ADR_O()] MUST be incremented, and the wrap size MUST be set by the burst type extension [BTE_O()] signals.

A MASTER signaling a constant address burst MUST initiate another cycle; the next cycle MUST be the same operation (either read or write), the select lines [SEL_O()] MUST have the same value, and the address array [ADR_O()] MUST have the same value.

The lock output [LOCK_O], when asserted, indicates that the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. Lock is asserted to request complete ownership of the bus. Once the transfer has started, the INTERCON does not grant the bus to any other MASTER until the current MASTER negates [LOCK_O] or [CYC_O].
The retry input [RTY_I] indicates that the interface is not ready to accept or send data, and that the cycle should be retried. When and how the cycle is retried is defined by the IP core supplier.
The error input [ERR_I] indicates an abnormal cycle termination. The source of the error, and the response generated by the MASTER is defined by the IP core supplier.

In pipelined mode the master does not wait for [ACK_I] before outputting the next address/data word; the [STALL_I] input indicates the slave pipeline cannot accept another request at the moment, and the master holds its requests as long as [STALL_I] is high.
In pipelined mode a read transaction is started when [CYC_I] and [STB_I] are asserted and [STALL_I] and [WE_I] are negated.
In pipelined mode a write transaction is started when [CYC_I], [STB_I] and [WE_I] are asserted and [STALL_I] is negated.
In pipelined mode the MASTER must accept [ACK_I] signals at any time after a transaction is initiated.

error_response_conditions: [ERR_I] asserted by SLAVE during a bus cycle terminates the cycle and notifies the MASTER that an error occurred (e.g. parity / address error). The MASTER's response is IP-supplier-defined.

[RTY_I] asserted by SLAVE during a bus cycle terminates the cycle and notifies the MASTER that the current cycle should be aborted and retried later. Typically used for shared memory and bus bridges that are temporarily busy.

protocol_overview.bus_role: Wishbone is a flexible MASTER/SLAVE on-chip interconnect for portable SoC IP cores. The protocol defines only the data-exchange signaling between MASTER and SLAVE; application-specific functions are outside the scope.
handshake_modes: Standard mode (asynchronous SLAVE — combinational [ACK_O] from [STB_I]+[CYC_I]) — Section 3.1.3.1
Pipelined mode (registered [ACK_O], [STALL_I] used to throttle master pipeline) — Section 3.1.3.2
Wishbone Registered Feedback bus cycles (Chapter 4) — uses [CTI_O()] + [BTE_O()] tags for advanced synchronous termination with bursts
protocol_overview.syscon_module: SYSCON generates [CLK_O] and [RST_O]; the INTERCON routes [CLK_O] -> all [CLK_I] inputs and [RST_O] -> all [RST_I] inputs of MASTERs and SLAVEs.

compliance_requirements: All MASTER interfaces MUST include at least [ACK_I], [CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], [STB_O] (RULE 3.40).
All SLAVE interfaces MUST include at least [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], [RST_I] (RULE 3.40).
All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active HIGH logic (RULE 2.30).
MASTER [CYC_O] MUST be asserted no later than the [STB_O] assertion and negated no earlier than the [STB_O] negation (RULE 3.25).
SLAVE MUST NOT assert more than one of [ACK_O] / [ERR_O] / [RTY_O] at any time (RULE 3.45).
Both MASTER and SLAVE MUST support the timing requirements of every cycle type they implement (RULE 3.75 / 3.80 / 3.85).
All Registered Feedback cores MUST also support Classic bus cycles (RULE 4.00).
User-defined tags MUST be assigned a TAG TYPE and MUST adhere to the timing of that TAG TYPE (RULE 3.70).
Data organization MUST conform to Figures 3-15, 3-18, 3-19, 3-20, 3-21 for the chosen port width (RULES 3.90 / 3.95 / 3.100 / 3.105 / 3.1010).

evidence.quote: All WISHBONE interfaces MUST initialize themselves at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I]. They MUST stay in the initialized state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I]. [RST_I] MUST be asserted for at least one complete clock cycle on all WISHBONE interfaces.

The following MASTER signals MUST be negated at the rising [CLK_I] edge following the assertion of [RST_I], and MUST stay in the negated state until the rising [CLK_I] edge that follows the negation of [RST_I]: [STB_O], [CYC_O]. The state of all other MASTER signals are undefined in response to a reset cycle.

MASTER interfaces MUST assert [CYC_O] for the duration of SINGLE READ / WRITE, BLOCK and RMW cycles. [CYC_O] MUST be asserted no later than the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the assertion of [STB_O]. [CYC_O] MUST be negated no earlier than the rising [CLK_I] edge that qualifies the negation of [STB_O].
SLAVE interfaces MAY NOT respond to any SLAVE signals when [CYC_I] is negated. However, SLAVE interfaces MUST always respond to SYSCON signals.
In standard mode the cycle termination signals [ACK_O], [ERR_O], and [RTY_O] must be generated in response to the logical AND of [CYC_I] and [STB_I].

As a minimum, the MASTER interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_I], [CLK_I], [CYC_O], [RST_I], and [STB_O]. As a minimum, the SLAVE interface MUST include the following signals: [ACK_O], [CLK_I], [CYC_I], [STB_I], and [RST_I]. All other signals are optional.
If a SLAVE supports the [ERR_O] or [RTY_O] signals, then the SLAVE MUST NOT assert more than one of the following signals at any time: [ACK_O], [ERR_O] or [RTY_O].
MASTER interfaces MUST qualify the following signals with [STB_O]: [ADR_O], [DAT_O()], [SEL_O()], [WE_O], and [TAGN_O].

In pipelined mode the master doesn't wait for [ACK_I] before outputting next address/data word on the bus. We have a [STALL_I] input in the master, indicating that the slave pipeline can accept another request at the moment. Master outputs the requests as long as [STALL_I] is low.

All WISHBONE Registered Feedback compatible cores MUST support WISHBONE Classic bus cycles. MASTER and SLAVE interfaces that do support the [CTI_I()] and [CTI_O()] signals MUST at least support the Classic cycle [CTI_IO()='000'] and the End-of-Cycle [CTI_IO()='111'].

A cycle terminates when both the cycle termination signal and [STB_I], [STB_O] is asserted. Even if [ACK_O], [ACK_I] is asserted, the other signals are only valid when [STB_O], [STB_I] is also asserted.
A MASTER MUST set End-Of-Burst to signal the end of the current burst.

A MASTER signaling an incrementing burst MUST initiate another cycle, the next cycle MUST be the same operation (either read or write), the select lines [SEL_O()] MUST have the same value, the address array [ADR_O()] MUST be incremented, and the wrap size MUST be set by the burst type extension [BTE_O()] signals.
